Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Budget squeeze — prioritization & batching path

Ethan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to make the next steps explicit.

Key pain points you shared:
- Q4 budget freeze across product teams; tight cap for any new infra spend.
- Rising token spend driven by long chat contexts and high concurrency during peak hours.
- Need predictable per-user cost and an ability to test cost levers before broader rollout.

Goals we discussed:
1) Short pilot (2–4 weeks) that demonstrates a clear TCO improvement while keeping latency within current SLOs.
2) Target: narrow a realistic savings band so Finance can decide on a pilot PO — preliminary aim: 25–40% unit-cost reduction depending on feature mix.
3) Minimal engineering lift for your frontend teams; Redwood handles batching/caching config and a simple SDK change.

Our suggested approach (high level):
- Phase 0 (this week): you send an anonymized usage sample (token-level distribution + request counts).
- Phase 1 (2-week canary): Redwood runs a canary on a small percentage of traffic with batching (configurable) + prefix/KV caching. We provide cost delta and latency breakdowns.
- Phase 2 (pilot extension): scale to larger subset if canary meets the savings/latency gates; deliver ROI model for 6 months.

Immediate asks / open items:
- Can you share a 7–14 day usage export (CSV) showing request timestamps, prompt length, response length, and route id? We attached a sample template (clearbank-usage-sample.csv).
- Procurement timeline & any mandatory contract clauses (data residency, SOC2 evidence).
- Target internal decision date (Finance / Product) so we can prioritize timing.

Attachments: clearbank-usage-sample.csv (template), Redwood pilot estimate (PDF).

Next steps I’ll take: I’ll have Ben produce a short technical note with expected savings ranges for the patterns you described, and Marissa will follow up on commercial terms.

If this summary looks right, I’ll schedule the canary kickoff for next Tue/Wed.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) Budget constraints: Finance has a Q4 hiring/hardware freeze; any new recurring spend needs a strong ROI case and Product sign-off. If your pilot can show a >25% net unit-cost reduction (including overhead for orchestration/observability), we can make a stronger case.
2) Data residency: we need confirmation that any logs/samples we share will remain within US regions and will be deleted after analysis unless otherwise agreed. SOC2 attestation and an IDS summary would help procurement.
3) Timeline: Procurement is swamped this month — earliest possible PO decision window looks like mid-November. A shorter canary (2 weeks) would be ideal so we can present results.

I’ll loop procurement on the usage sample question. Attaching a couple of notes from our side (not included here).

Ethan — quick technical note on the levers we discussed (attached as batching-cache-savings-notes.txt). High-level: 

- Batching: aggregating short requests into micro-batches at the inference layer typically reduces per-token overhead. For chat-heavy traffic with average prompt+response lengths ~600 tokens, batching factor of 4–8 can yield ~15–30% cost reduction on GPU-backed pipelines depending on latency SLAs.
- KV/prefix caching: for workflows where prompts share a stable system+instruction prefix or repeated user context, KV cache can capture repeated KV states and avoid recomputation — we’ve seen 10–25% additional token reduction on conversational workloads.
- Combined effect: in preliminary tests similar to the pattern you described, combined batching + cache reductions landed in the 28–45% range. Spread depends on concurrency distribution and tail latencies.

Operational notes:
- Canary config: we recommend starting at 5% of traffic with a single model variant, measure per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and token-cost delta.
- Safety: no prompt content is stored beyond the short-term cache; we can run on a private tenancy for the pilot if you want to limit exposure.

I’ll join the kickoff call if you want to go over the config.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Next actions I’ll take this week:
- Share SOW + simple addendum for the pilot (DocuSign link included).
- Schedule the technical kickoff contingent on receipt of the usage sample (we can run an anonymized export).

Ethan — is mid-November still the internal decision target? If so we’ll prioritize the deliverables for the end of the canary so your Finance review has a crisp ROI line.

Thanks —
